recon.notes: Squarespace, static: each of the parser's two urls IS one listing — a single announcement block rewritten per party (the home page for the San Francisco edition, /brooklyn for the New York edition). Neither page prints a year: "SATURDAY, SEPT 26" matches 2026-09-26 (a Saturday, the eve of Folsom Street Fair 2026 — what "FOLSOM" refers to) and "SATURDAY SEPTEMBER 19" matches 2026-09-19 (a Saturday, the recon date itself, so the Brooklyn party is the night of the read). The ra.co and DICE ticket pages would settle year, door time and price but were not opened (no network on the recon date). Neither page states a recurrence for the party itself. 2026-09-29: the site announces each party on a page of its own and its menu lists them — the home page still shows the Folsom party of Sept 26 (over), the menu item "Halloween" leads to /grunt-halloween (Oct 24). Run 20260929-091555 read 0 upcoming because a page that reads as one event followed no menu link; the crawl now opens the other pages of a single-event root's own site.

coverage.basis: One event per page. Home-page door (https://gruntparty.monster/, cached copy of 2026-09-27): the Folsom party, Saturday Sept 26 at The Stud, one ra.co ticket link. Brooklyn door (https://gruntparty.monster/brooklyn, cached copy of 2026-09-27): Saturday September 19 at C'mon Everybody, one DICE ticket link. Halloween door (https://gruntparty.monster/grunt-halloween, fetched 2026-09-29, linked from the header nav): Saturday Oct 24 at The Stud, 9pm-2am. Published = 3 singles, 1 of them upcoming on 2026-09-29. Confidence is medium rather than high because no page prints a year and the ticket pages that would confirm it were not opened.

traps.label: "BROOKLYN" in the header nav (href="/brooklyn") on the home page, and "FOLSOM" (href="/") on /brooklyn
traps.why: Each page's header nav links to the other edition's page; the nav item carries no date, venue or ticket link, so it is not an event on the page it appears on. Each party is documented from its own page only — the Brooklyn night from /brooklyn, the Folsom night from / — never from the cross-link.
traps.note: The nav is rendered three times in each page's source (desktop, mobile, and the mobile overlay), so a text-window reader sees "FOLSOM | BROOKLYN" three times before the announcement. Since both urls are in the parser's config, a run should yield exactly one record per page, not a Folsom ghost from /brooklyn or vice versa. 2026-09-29: the menu is the site's list of its parties and changes with them (FOLSOM | BROOKLYN on 2026-09-19, FOLSOM | Halloween on 2026-09-27). A menu item is still not an event on the page it appears on; the page it leads to is read as a page of its own.

openQuestions.q: Neither page prints a year. 2026 is inferred from the weekday match (Sept 26 and September 19 are both Saturdays in 2026) and from the Folsom Street Fair context; the ra.co (2447663) and DICE (j1e6d0b77886) ticket pages were not opened and would confirm year, door time and price.

Should the event titles be "GRUNT FOLSOM" / "GRUNT BROOKLYN" (site name + the page's edition label) or just "GRUNT"? The pages print no event name beyond those words; the ticket listings' titles (unread) may settle it.

The parser lists / and /brooklyn by hand. /brooklyn has left the site's menu and still shows the September 19 party; the crawl now follows the menu of a single-event root by itself, so the home page alone would reach every page the site lists. Whether to drop /brooklyn from the configured urls is the owner's call (it costs one request per refresh and returns a past event until the page is rewritten).
